title: Control traceability notes: RBACv2 + SIEM export mapping
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working notes doc to help prepare SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence for auditor review focused on three converging areas: RBAC v2 role design and enforcement, audit log schema (ingestion/export), and SIEM export traces used as evidence. The goal: produce a minimal, defensible trace from user/role change -> enforcement -> audit event -> SIEM export.

Audience:
- Security & Compliance reviewers
- Eng owners for RBAC, audit logging, SIEM integration
- Solutions for auditor Q&A prep

High-level objectives (what we need to show auditors):
1) Control mapping: for each SOC 2 CC/ISO control clause we must show where RBAC, logging, and SIEM outputs provide coverage.
2) Traceability: example chain showing a privileged role change and how it is recorded and exported.
3) Gap list + remediation owners and timeline.
4) Auditor Q&A script + sample queries to pull evidence quickly.

Current assumptions / context (do not rely on until validated):
- RBAC v2 rollout began Aug 2024, majority of services migrated but a few legacy admin endpoints still use role aliasing.
- Central audit service emits JSON lines to our SIEM (Kafka -> SIEM) with schema v1.3; a migration to v2 (more structured actor/actor_id/action/resource_type) is in progress (owner: Diego).
- SIEM export retains 90 days hot, 365 days cold; SOC 2 scope requires 12 months retention for selected evidence (we use snapshot export for T3 evidence).

Control mapping (working table notes):
- SOC 2: CC6 (Logical and physical access controls) -> RBAC enforcement (role assignment, approval workflow, periodic recertification).
  Evidence: RBAC change log event, approval ticket link, access review spreadsheet export, proof of enforcement (failed access attempt + allowed when role present).
- SOC 2: CC7 (System operations and availability) -> Audit logs showing admin config changes and deployment events (for changes that affect security controls).
  Evidence: audit logs (config-change events) + deployment CI job links.
- ISO 27001: A.9 (Access control) -> RBAC policy docs + actual policy enforcement logs + periodic review records.
  Evidence: policy doc in Confluence, RBAC assignment CSV export, access review signoff.

RBAC v2 specific trace points to capture: (these should all be present in the audit stream)
- role.created / role.updated / role.deleted: include role_id, role_name, actor, change_reason, ticket_id
- role.binding.created / role.binding.removed: mapping user_id/group_id -> role_id, timestamp, actor
- permission.grant/permission.revoke: low-level permission changes (if present)
- authz.evaluation.failed and authz.evaluation.allowed: when a request is denied/allowed, include policy_version and cache_hit boolean

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields) - proposed v2 mapping (flattened JSON fields to map to SIEM indexes):
- ts (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- actor_type (user/service/automation)
- actor_id (email/service-account)
- actor_role_ids (list)
- action (string, e.g. role.binding.created)
- resource_type (role,user,project,model)
- resource_id
- outcome (success/failure)
- ip_address
- user_agent
- request_id
- policy_version
- change_request_id (optional - links to ticket)
- raw_payload (truncated)

SIEM export considerations (how auditors will want to see it):
- Provide a CSV export of focused fields for the time window: ts,event_id,actor_id,action,resource_type,resource_id,outcome,change_request_id
- Include a short README describing indexing and timezone normalization (all timestamps are UTC)
- For privacy, redact PII where required but maintain stable IDs so the chain is reconstructable (e.g., use hashed_user_id with salt stored in a secure vault)

Example trace (minimal reproducible chain) - capture of a role change and enforcement:
1) Ticket: JIRA-SEC-7431 created (access request)
2) Actor admin@redwood approves in console -> system emits role.binding.created with change_request_id=JIRA-SEC-7431 and actor_id=admin@redwood
3) Audit service writes JSON line to kafka: {ts, event_id, actor_id, action: "role.binding.created", resource_type: "role", resource_id: "role-3", change_request_id: "JIRA-SEC-7431"}
4) SIEM ingests and indexes the event; export CSV for date range includes the row above
5) To prove enforcement: run a sample request from user@redwood who previously had different role -> see authz.evaluation.allowed after binding applied, earlier authz.evaluation.failed present (within same trace chain via request_id correlation)

Sample auditor Q&A script (quick responses + where to pull):
Q: How do you control who can grant privileged roles?
A: RBAC v2 enforces separation: only members of role admin-iam can perform role.binding.* operations. Evidence: export of role.binding.created events filtered by action + change_request_id; attached policy doc (Confluence). Pull query: "action:role.binding.created AND resource_id:role-* AND outcome:success | fields actor_id, change_request_id, ts"

Q: How do you demonstrate periodic access review?
A: We have quarterly access review snapshots stored in s3://redwood-compliance/access-reviews/{YYYY}-{Q}.csv. Evidence: signed spreadsheet (access-review-Q3-2024.csv) and a sample SIEM export showing role assignment differences pre/post review.

Q: Can you produce an end-to-end sample that ties a ticket to a privileged action and a subsequent enforcement?
A: Yes (see the example trace above). For the auditor we prepare a package: ticket pdf, CSV export of audit events for the time window, brief play-by-play doc mapping rows to steps.

Known gaps (short) and proposed fixes (owner / ETA):
- No standard change_request_id on older audit events (legacy). Fix: retrospective mapping via ticket references in message text (Diego, Q2 2025).
- SIEM export CSV profile missing policy_version field; required for proving which policy was used at decision time. Fix: add policy_version to export contract (Liam, 2025-01-31).
- Automated snapshot for 12-month auditor package not yet implemented (we currently do manual exports). Fix: automation runbook + job in infra to generate monthly compliance snapshots to long-term storage (Zara, 2025-02-28).

Evidence packaging checklist (for this control area):
- [ ] RBAC policy doc (Confluence) with version and owner
- [ ] Role assignment export (CSV) with timestamped bindings for scope
- [ ] SIEM CSV export for the selected time window (fields: ts,event_id,actor_id,action,resource_type,resource_id,outcome,change_request_id)
- [ ] Ticket PDF(s) for any change requests used as evidence
- [ ] Access review snapshot and signoff artifact
- [ ] Play-by-play mapping doc (this helps auditors navigate the exports)

Operational runbook notes (how to pull during audit):
- Preferred path: compliance-scripts repo -> scripts/export-siem-window.sh --start YYYY-MM-DD --end YYYY-MM-DD --fields ts,event_id,actor_id,action,resource_type,resource_id,outcome,change_request_id -> outputs CSV to /tmp/evidence.zip
- If SIEM UI is needed: Kibana saved search "rbac-trace-export-v1" (owner: Liam Chen)
- For RBAC inventory: run admin console export -> Admin -> Roles -> Export (CSV)

Open questions / decisions required (action owners):
- Retention: confirm that snapshot retention 12 months cold meets ISO auditors (Legal/SecOps - Priya)
- PII redaction policy: finalize hash+salt approach and where salt is kept (Security - Zara)
- When do we flip audit schema to v2 (Diego) - roll-forward vs backfill strategy (audit requirement: must tie change_request_id for auditor package).

Appendix: Sample Kibana-esque query examples
- Find role changes for role-3 in window:
  event.action:role.binding.created AND resource_id:role-3 AND @timestamp:[2024-09-01 TO 2024-09-30]
- Correlate request failure -> later success by same request_id:
  request_id: "abcd-1234" | sort @timestamp asc

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc as the "go-to" for auditor pull; link to it from audit playbook page.
- When packaging, include a short README for the auditor that lists the exact commands used to extract CSV rows (so they can verify reproducibility).

References and pointers:
- Confluence: /spaces/SEC/pages/42322/RBACv2+Design (draft)
- Github schema PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-schemas/pull/18 (contains proposed v2)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-7342 (SIEM export contract)

-- end of notes --
